blue-catfish: Fishing for a mix of blue catfish and channel catfish is good this week.
Anglers are using various types of cut bait, and some anglers are using live bait to target the largest blue catfish.
In the lower Bay tidal rivers, it seems there will always be blue catfish.
channel-catfish: Fishing for a mix of blue catfish and channel catfish is good this week.
largemouth-bass: Freshwater Fishing Harrison Moroz holds up a 21-inch largemouth bass he caught and released from Deep Creek Lake this past weekend.
Largemouth bass will be doing the same in the many nontidal and tidal waters throughout the state.
Maryland DNR fisheries biologists Ryan Gary and Joseph Love collaborated with Major League Fishing to publish a research paper on live image sonar (LIS) and its use when largemouth bass fishing.
smallmouth-bass: Anglers are enjoying exciting fishing for smallmouth bass in the upper Potomac River, Deep Creek Lake, and several central region reservoirs this month.
striped-bass: Upper Chesapeake Bay Lucy Moore holds up a pair of striped bass she and her dad caught while fishing the Susquehanna Flats over the weekend.

Photo by Nick Perez Cooler water temperatures are turning up the fishing action for striped bass anglers casting paddletails and topwater lures in the shallower waters, especially near the edges of the Susquehanna Flats and structured…
Baitfish in the form of juvenile menhaden are moving out of the major tidal rivers into the upper Bay, and into a gauntlet of hungry striped bass hoping to put on some weight after a long hot summer.
white-perch: Small white perch and bluegill sunfish are common choices for live bait.
White perch are heading deep and can be found in the middle to lower sections of the tidal rivers this week.
Kent Narrows is another good place to check for striped bass and white perch this time of the year.

rig.primary: 3/8 oz round jighead (2/0) with 3.5-4 in white or chartreuse paddletail/grub, 20 lb braid to 3 ft 12 lb fluoro

rig.switch_trigger: Snagging every cast in rock, or fish seen chasing near the surface at dusk
rig.gear_note: Workable on Matt's 7 ft Crossfire MH (20 lb braid) with the leader dropped to 10-12 lb; ideal is a 6'6"-7' medium spinning rod with 10 lb braid. The unconfirmed 6'6" Ugly Stik fits if the 17 lb leader is swapped lighter.
